Subject: POC environment onboarding — network & identity ownership (target close 2026-09-10)

Hi Alice / Jim —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our call, I pulled together a concise next-steps summary to lock the MAP milestone for POC environment readiness. Goal: have the sandbox environment accessible to your engineers and a first test run by the week of 2026-09-06, with a soft target close of 2026-09-10 for the POC kickoff.

Summary of dependencies we agreed on (high level):
- VPC peering (ACME -> Redwood VPC) and routing updates
- IP allowlist entries for Redwood egress and public API endpoints
- SSO/SAML integration (IdP metadata + test user)
- Secrets/KMS access pattern (Customer-managed keys or allowlist for Redwood service principal)

Action request (please confirm owners & rough ETAs by EOD Friday):
1) VPC peering owner at your side + preferred peering window
2) Network person who will provide IP ranges (CIDR list) for allowlisting
3) SSO contact who can share IdP metadata and a test account
4) Security/KMS contact who can confirm whether you want Redwood to use Customer-managed KMS or an isolated secret inject flow

I'm attaching a lightweight network diagram and a draft MAP workbook with the milestone rows prefilled. Note: on the Redwood side, Karthik will own infra setup and Ben will coordinate the test plan and success criteria.

If you'd prefer a short working session to run through the checklist together, we can do a 30-minute call early next week — propose Tue 2026-08-17 10:00-10:30 PT.

Cheers,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks Sofia — helpful summary. Quick answers from our side: 

1) VPC peering: owner is Jim Patel (infra@acmecorp.com). Preferred peering window: 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-26 (we can open a maintenance window in that range).
2) IP allowlist: I can consolidate the CIDRs; expect that by 2026-08-16 EOD.
3) SSO/SAML: IAM team will provide IdP metadata and a test user. Point-of-contact: Rachel Wu (rachel.wu@bankingcorp.com). ETA: 2026-08-18.
4) KMS/secrets: Security prefers Customer-managed KMS. I'll loop in security owner (cc'd Jim for infra, but will add security contact after confirmation).

We should also confirm data residency constraints — our compliance team requires logs to remain in us-east-1 for the POC. Is Redwood able to pin the POC infra to us-east-1?

Happy to take the 30-min call on Tue 2026-08-17 10:00 PT. If that works for your team, please send the invite.

Best,
Alice

Thanks Alice — clear and appreciated. Quick notes from infra side: 

- We can pin the POC to us-east-1. We'll stand up a dedicated VPC with restricted subnet ranges; peering with your VPC is fine.
- For peering maintenance window, please confirm the exact cutover hour (we recommend a 2-hour window starting on the hour) and whether you require route table propagation immediately or after validation.
- IP ranges: once you share CIDRs we'll update the security groups/NAT rules and provide you a test endpoint IP.
- SSO/SAML: we support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. If you can share metadata, we'll prepare a test assertion endpoint and a test user.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys work. We'll need the key ARN and a cross-account grant (we can provide the IAM principal that requires the grant). If you prefer not to grant direct KMS access, we can use a sealed secret flow — discuss with your security team which is preferable.

To keep the MAP clean, I've added rows to the workbook (attached) with the following proposed owners & due dates: 
- VPC peering: Jim Patel (due 2026-08-24)
- IP allowlist: Alice Morgan (due 2026-08-16)
- SSO metadata: Rachel Wu / IAM (due 2026-08-18)
- KMS decision: BankingCorp Security (due 2026-08-20)

I'll join the Tue 2026-08-17 10:00 PT call to coordinate the peering plan and test cutover steps.

Cheers,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
